#2766. Jaguars stunned by Giants amid officiating controversy, questionable late-game decision from head coach Liam Coen

The Jacksonville Jaguars entered Sunday at 7-2 having emerged as a Super Bowl favorite out of the AFC.

The New York Giants doused them with a splash of cold water.

Plagued by red-zone woes, officiating controversy and a questionable late-game decision by Jacksonville head coach Liam Coen, the Jaguars fell 23-18 to the Giants.

Jacksonville had a shot to tie the game with fourth-and-goal at the New York 8-yard line and 3:40 remaining on the clock. New York led 23-15, and the Jaguars were down to one timeout.

But instead of going for a potential game-tying touchdown and 2-point conversion, Coen opted to kick a field goal that cut the deficit to five points, apparently betting on the Jaguars' defense to get them the ball back.

Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars suffered a stunning loss to the Giants on Sunday.

They did not. Cam Skattebo ran for a first down before the two-minute warning with the Jaguars having exhausted their final timeout. The Giants were able to kneel out the remaining two minutes of game clock in victory formation.

It added up to a jarring loss for the now 7-3 Jaguars on the heels of an aggressive trade deadline in which they made several big swings to bolster their hopes of a Super Bowl run. The Giants, meanwhile, improved to 6-3-1 to maintain their lead in the NFC East over the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys.

Coen was asked about his decision to kick the late field goal in his postgame news conference. He cited analytics charts and described going for a touchdown as a "hope play."

"We talked about it a few times," Coen said. "Our defense, they hadn't done anything up until that point. Everything about the charts and everything talked about it said kick the field goal, get within five points.

"Go get a stop, and you feel pretty good about where you're at. Just executing that down-and-distance on a fourth down is kinda challenging. Especially, they're zero blitzing you every play, the ball's gonna come out. It's like a hope play."

Coen's comments Sunday stood in contrast to a previous discussion with Barstool Sports about a strikingly similar, but not identical hypothetical scenario.

In that discussion, Coen was asked about whether to kick a field goal or go for it when down by eight points at the 8-yard line with one key caveat: "When you're up against the greatest quarterback of all time."

"You've gotta go for it," Coen said. … "It's weird down there — and you're in an opportunity to score a touchdown, you're that close. We all know how hard it is to score in the red zone in this league. … I think you've gotta be aggressive there."

Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy is certainly not "the greatest quarterback of all time." It's not clear if Coen would have made a different decision if facing a different caliber of quarterback.

The Giants were in control virtually from the start. They took a 10-3 advantage into the second quarter and a 20-6 lead into halftime. While McCarthy kept New York's offense moving and scoring, the Jaguars repeatedly broke down in the red zone.

Jacksonville's first three trips to the red zone produced 6 points courtesy of two field goals and a turnover on downs in the third quarter when a fourth-and-1 pass from Trevor Lawrence fell incomplete.

Jacksonville's fourth red-zone trip produced controversy on a third-down effort to cut their deficit to one possession.

They appeared to do just that when Parker Washington made a leaping catch in the back of the end zone and got both feet in bounds. But officials ruled that he didn't maintain control of the ball as he hit the ground.

Coen used Jacksonville's last remaining challenge to challenge the call on the field. The ball moved in Washington's hands after Washington hit the ground, but he never appeared to lose control of it.

But officials didn't see enough to overturn the call on the field, and the ruling of an incomplete pass stood. The result was a fourth down in which the Jaguars settled for a field goal to cut their deficit to 20-9.

Jacksonville finally cracked the end zone with a touchdown pass from Lawrence to Brian Thomas Jr. with 6:39 remaining. A failed 2-point conversion left the Jaguars facing a 23-15 hole.

Then came the decision that will prompt plenty of questions for Coen.

In the end, the Jaguars woke up on offense and limited the Giants on defense as they outgained New York, 354 yards to 238. Lawrence completed 25 of 47 passes for 301 yards with 1 touchdown and 2 interceptions.

McCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with 1 touchdown. But he didn't turn the ball over as the Giants won the takeaway battle, 2 to 1.

The result will leave the Jaguars with plenty to ponder ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Titans.

The Giants do indeed have the ability to run the clock out.

The discussion for this game will be Jacksonville focused. First it will be whether or not Parker Washington deserved a touchdown on his reception in the end zone that was ruled incomplete.

The second will be Liam Coen's decision to be on the 8-yard line facing fourth down and opting to kick a meaningless field goal rather than trying to tie the game.

Giants running back Cam Skattebo said that he was retiring the backflip after what happened to Aidan Hutchinson tearing his ACL celebrating a sack.

Skattebo picked up the first down at the two-minute warning. Jacksonville has no timeouts left, so this should be the ball game.

The Giants running back celebrated the only way he knew how: with a backflip.

The Giants are in the driver's seat needing a few first downs to seal with win against the Jaguars.

On second and seven, JJ McCarthy hit rookie wideout Malachi Fields for the 19-yard gain. Jacksonville only has one timeout left.

The Jaguars were grooving down the field, but the offense stalled in the red zone. After several incompletions by Trevor Lawrence to the end zone, Jacksonville opted to kick the field goal.

Cam Little connected on the 26-yard field goal. Jacksonville now trails 23-18 with 3:40 left.

After an incompletion on first down, JJ McCarthy hit Malik Nabers for an eight-yard gain. An offensive lineman was then whistled for unnecessary roughness for hitting a Jaguars defender late.

After another incompletion, New York was forced to punt.

Jacksonville gets the ball back down 8 with 5:47 left to go in regulation.

It looked like it was going to be a broken play as Trevor Lawrence had time, but couldn't find anybody.

All of a sudden he fired it to the end zone and Brian Thomas Jr. had gotten wide open.

Jacksonville decided to go for two. He floated it into the end zone but it was picked, which doesn't mean much for the stat sheet other than the attempt failed.

New York leads 23-15 with 6:39 left to go.

Giants rookie kicker Dominic Zvada had made a 53-yard field goal and missed a 32-yarder.

Zvada lined up for a 43-yard attempt and drilled it.

New York leads 23-9 with 10 minutes to go.

He had an incompletion on first down, and then threw his second interception of the game.

The officials in this game are certainly apparent.

New York picked up seven yards on first down, but it was called back due to offensive holding.

JJ McCarthy then had three consecutive incompletions. New York took 1:02 off the clock and punted back to Jacksonville.

The Giants lead 20-9 with 11:15 left in the game.

It looked like Parker Washington made his latest video game-esque catch, but it was ruled an incompletion.

Replay on the broadcast had JJ Watt swearing that it was a touchdown. Even the rules analyst on the broadcast said it should have been a touchdown. Jacksonville challenged the play and the ruling was upheld.

While the Jaguars didn't get a touchdown out of it, Jacksonville did add three with a field goal.

New York leads 20-9 with 12:17 left in the game.

New York's drive consisted of two incompletions and then JJ McCarthy scrambling for a massive 29-yard gain.

On third and 16 McCarthy had his third incompletion of the drive and New York was forced to punt.

Jacksonville takes over trailing 20-6 at the start of the fourth quarter.

Jacksonville got down to the 11-yard line. Trailing 20-6 with a minute to go in the third quarter, Liam Coen opted to go for it.

Trevor Lawrence stared down his target and tried to thread the needle to Jakobi Meyers, but the Giants defense was all over it for the turnover on downs.

The Jaguars defense had been on the field for over five minutes. Jacksonville needing something and it came in the form of a Cam Skattebo fumble.

Jacksonville scooped it, and the defender spun away from the line and took it back 42 yards to give the Jaguars great field position.

Jacksonville couldn't capitalize on New York's missed field goal. Trevor Lawrence had two incompletions sandwiching a one-yard gain by Bhayshul Tuten.

New York leads 20-6 with 9 minutes to go in the third quarter.

Rookie kicker Dominic Zvada had made a 53-yard field goal already in the game. It looked like his 32-yard attempt was going to be easy, but he planted weird and ended up pushing it wide left.

Giants head coach John Harbaugh is showing he trusts his rookie kicker.

Dominic Zvada has been inconsistent this season, but nailed a 54-yarder toward the end of the first half to put the Giants up 20-6.

Trevor Lawrence put on a magic show in the backfield. He eluded three different sets of pressure from the Giants and managed to get a pass off.

Brenton Strange caught it even though it wasn't nearly enough for the first down, it was still impressive. It ended up being just a gain of four.

After the two-minute warning, Jacksonville punted trailing 17-6.

This might be Abdul Carter's breakout game. He has found a mismatch on the Jaguars' offensive line because he is consistently going after Trevor Lawrence in the backfield.

Carter already has two sacks in the game and four tackles overall.

New York drove the field against the Jacksonville defense.

The Giants' nine-play, 66-yard touchdown drive ends with JJ McCarthy finding Malik Nabers in the back of the end zone as the wide receiver just manages to get his two touches in.

Jacksonville's offensive drive stalled in the red zone. The drive was highlighted by a nice 21-yard grab by Parker Washington.

On third and 12, Trevor Lawrence fumbled the snap, but was able to recover it. He couldn't find anything downfield and took off. He only picked up 8 yards.

Cam Little came on and nailed the 35-yard field goal to decrease the Giants' lead to four points.

New York leads 10-6 early in the second quarter.

#2765. Chelsea make Xabi Alonso sack decision after Leeds United humiliation at Stamford Bridge

Xabi Alonso is facing the first major crisis of his Chelsea tenure after a humiliating 4-1 home defeat to Leeds United sparked a furious reaction from the Stamford Bridge faithful. Despite the growing unrest, the Blues hierarchy have delivered a definitive verdict on the Spaniard's immediate future in the dugout.

Saturday's 4-1 defeat against bitter rivals Leeds ended the visitors' 27-year wait for a Premier League win in west London. Loud boos echoed around the stadium at full-time as frustrated supporters voiced their anger.

That setback marked a third loss in four league matches, leaving Chelsea stuck in mid-table and short on belief. Alonso's side have suffered five defeats overall while conceding an alarming 20 goals in 11 games.

Yet according to Mail Sport, club executives will not make a hasty call to dismiss the 44-year-old. Despite his honeymoon period ending abruptly, boardroom figures are unwilling to pull the trigger so early in his reign.

Luring Alonso this summer was viewed as a major coup. Chelsea beat Liverpool and Manchester City to the former Real Madrid boss' signature while both rivals hunted replacements for their outgoing managers.

Heavy investment fuelled title expectations, especially without European football as a distraction. Although results have faltered, Alonso is not yet facing the intense pressure that quickly overwhelmed predecessors Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior, who lasted mere months in charge.

Romeo Lavia acknowledged the squad's frustration after surrendering control at home. "Everyone is very angry and disappointed," Lavia told the club's official website. "At home this is never the way you want to finish a game. We let them back in the game when we shouldn't have. This is something we will analyse and get better at."

Still, Lavia insisted the players remain committed to Alonso's vision. "When we won games, when we lost games, we always said that no matter what, it's a process," he added. "With these types of results, it feels like the end of the world, but we are not going to ring the bell now to say it's a panic moment. Not at all. We are very confident as a team. We know where we want to get to."

He also backed the setback to spark an immediate response, concluding: "This hurts. It needs to hurt so it provokes a reaction from the team, and this is definitely going to help us for the next game on Friday."

Chelsea have little time to dwell on their defensive lapses before visiting Nottingham Forest's City Ground on Friday night. Fixing the errors that allowed Leeds back into the contest will be Alonso's priority as he works to restore fragile confidence.

With the hierarchy offering breathing room for now, the players must turn their anger into a sharper display on the road. Delivering a strong response against Forest is vital if Alonso is to quieten the growing unrest.

#2763. Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double

Observations after Sixers beat Bucks to move to 3-0, Embiid posts triple-double originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers stayed unbeaten Saturday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, earning a 127-116 win over the Bucks and improving to 3-0 on the season.

Joel Embiid had his 10th career regular-season triple-double, tallying 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists.

On his 30th birthday, Jaylen Brown posted 27 points and five assists. Tyrese Maxey had 26 points. VJ Edgecombe scored 17 and grabbed 13 boards.

The Sixers' absences on the first night of a back-to-back included LeBron James (low back/sciatica management). Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said pregame that he did not know yet who would be available for his team's matchup with the Pistons on Sunday.

Here are observations on the Sixers' victory Saturday:

Dean Wade made his Sixers debut and started in James' place. He'd missed the first two games of the regular season with a left ankle sprain.

The 3-and-D forward scored the night's first points by a sinking a corner three-pointer on the opening possession.

Embiid also had a sharp start. He moved well, made good decisions and served as the main hub of his team's offense in the early going.

The Sixers' seven-time All-Star center has often enjoyed facing Myles Turner. He entered the night with an average of 29.4 points in 18 previous games against the Bucks big man.

Embiid did a little bit of everything in the first quarter, posting eight points, four assists and four rebounds over nine minutes. After snatching an offensive board, Embiid drained a fadeaway jumper to give the Sixers a 10-1 lead.

One of Embiid's assists was quite stylish. He found Edgecombe open beyond the arc with a behind-the-back bounce pass. Edgecombe knocked down the shot and wound up going 3 for 4 from three-point range in the first quarter.

The Sixers added rookie Labaron Philon Jr. to their rotation. Jabari Walker stayed in the mix, though he didn't enter until the 7:36 mark of the second quarter.

Philon played four minutes in his NBA debut and missed his lone shot attempt, a corner three. On defense, Philon allowed a couple of blow-bys off the dribble. He generally looked like he belonged on offense, albeit without any production in his brief run.

Maxey banked in a half-court heave at the first-quarter buzzer to put the Sixers up nine points. The Sixers couldn't carry forward any momentum, however, and began the second quarter poorly.

Adem Bona had another rough stint amid a subpar start to the season. After Anfernee Simons missed a transition layup try, Ryan Rollins' three lifted the Bucks into a 40-37 lead.

The dreadful stretch for the Sixers on both sides of the ball called to mind how they'd fallen into a 29-point deficit Thursday night vs. the Cavaliers before clawing out a comeback win.

The Sixers mustered just seven points in first six minutes of the second quarter and had many stagnant possessions that concluded with contested jumpers. The team's transition defense was dismal for much of the second period. Milwaukee had the game's first 19 fast-break points.

The Sixers regained the lead late in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope made two three-balls in the second and nabbed three first-half steals. Embiid assisted a go-ahead, and-one Walker layup.

Brown hit a three with 11.8 seconds left in the second quarter. Unsurprisingly, his variety of shotmaking skills were useful without James in the lineup.

Even when James or Embiid sit, the Sixers should have a simple advantage in terms of volume of stars over most opponents this year. None of Brown, Embiid or Maxey had the sort of off night that would have improved the Bucks' odds of a road win. They'd all passed the 20-point mark by the end of the third quarter.

Maxey notched another final-possession bucket, this time with a more conventional make. He canned a jumper from the right elbow with 1.7 seconds left in the third to extend the Sixers' lead to 97-87.

The Bucks made a late push in the fourth quarter. Kel'el Ware's put-back, and-one layup cut the Milwaukee's deficit to 117-114.

The Sixers ultimately handled business. Embiid reached his triple-double by assisting a second-chance Brown jumper and and Caldwell-Pope soon drilled a dagger corner three. Embiid even threw down a last-minute dunk for good measure.

For the second consecutive season, the Sixers have a 3-0 start. They got to four wins last year before dropping their first game.

#2760. As Anthropic shares tank, investors scramble to hedge. It could be very expensive

As Anthropic shares tumble toward their IPO price of $83, investors are looking for ways to hedge. Unfortunately, they may have to wait until Monday, when options on the AI giant are expected to list.

If Anthropic breaks its IPO price, it will represent a 27% decline from Thursday's intraday high of $113. The wild price swings offer clues on how expensive it might be to buy protection on the new tech giant once options begin trading.A 20% intraday move points to an implied volatility somewhere between 100 and 150 for Anthropic options, according to estimates from single-stock market-makers on the Cboe trading floor in Chicago.

Options traders are also looking at how SpaceX traded in the days following its offering for clues on how options might price.

Implied volatility in SpaceX started at 116, but that didn't deter options traders big and small from piling into the contracts tracking the stock, with about 1.7 million contracts traded on the first day for a total options premium of about $2.5 billion. Far out-of-the-money call contracts were some of the most popular trades as the stock soared 40% in its first three sessions.One key difference between now and then? Anthropic is trading against the backdrop of S&P 500 volatility close to 30, compared to 17.3 when SpaceX debuted. "I expect ANT options to be super active," said Tom Sosnoff, co-founder of the trading platforms ThinkOrSwim and TastyTrade. "I expect heavy options volume."One thing Anthropic and SpaceX have in common is heavy retail involvement in both IPOs, with retail brokerages receiving a 20% allocation from SpaceX and reports pointing to between a 15-20% allocation from Anthropic on Thursday. "Round one of the Anthropic IPO easily goes to the individual investor," Sosnoff added. "Retail participants bailed early at the best prices of the day while institutional investors paid up to top off their underwhelming allocations. I believe retail was aggressively reloading in the mid-90s."Further signs of retail demand will become evident when options likely begin trading on Monday. One thing to watch: the spread between out-of-the-money call and put contracts, which was heavily skewed toward calls in the case of SpaceX. "I would be careful comparing Anthropic to SpaceX," said Dennis Davitt, CIO and Co-Founder of Millbank Dartmoor Portsmouth. "From a market-structure perspective, the two are dramatically different. The availability and cost of borrowing will be different, the companies are at very different stages of maturity, and SpaceX has allowed employees to monetize portions of their holdings over time. All of those factors matter when pricing options."

#2757. Bruins Lose Out on Dylan Larkin as Arch-Rival Canadiens Land 3-Time All-Star

The Boston Bruins lost out on Dylan Larkin on Sunday, when the Detroit Red Wings sent the center to the Montreal Canadiens, the Bruins' fiercest NHL rival, going back to 1924.

The Canadiens landed a 30-year-old who scored 30 goals in five straight seasons, and the Bruins, who spent weeks waiting for an opening, now have to look elsewhere.

Montreal sent Kirby Dach, goalie Samuel Montembeault, the rights to top prospect Michael Hage and four draft picks, including two first-rounders, to Detroit. Larkin had to approve it, and he did, when he waived his no-trade clause for the trade, according to ESPN.

The deal ended a standoff that began when Larkin asked out of Detroit. The Red Wings stripped Larkin of the captaincy and suspended him without pay, and he forfeited more than $1 million in salary before a trade got done.

Brutal Bruins-Hurricanes Fight Caught on Video: Watch Deslauriers Battle Jeannot

The Bruins never made it onto Larkin's list. They weren't among the 10 teams on Larkin's approved list, and neither were the Canadiens.

That didn't keep Boston out of the conversation. TSN's Darren Dreger reported that Detroit pro scouting director Kris Draper attended a Bruins game in Boston, and that general managers Don Sweeney of the Bruins and Kent Hughes of the Canadiens were "very eager to get involved," as quoted by the Boston Globe. Dreger also said Boston would love to make a deal for Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson, "probably more so than Dylan Larkin," as quoted by NBC Sports Boston.

"I suspect Boston, honestly, is another one," Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman said on 32 Thoughts, referring to teams hoping he would. Friedman added that "they don't lose," and cited a plus-20 goal differential through 16 games.

Not everyone saw a path. The Athletic's Fluto Shinzawa expected Boston to look into a deal but doubted the Bruins had enough trade capital, according to The Hockey News. A Bruins Mafia account later claimed Boston had tabled a package built around Pavel Zacha plus picks that Detroit preferred to other bids. No outlet confirmed it. Minnesota reportedly offered Danila Yurov and three first-round picks, according to the Detroit Free Press.

What would it have cost? One outside projection floated Zacha, Matthew Poitras and Mason Lohrei, plus a first-round pick and a prospect such as Will Zellers or Cooper Simpson, according to Boston.com. The same projection named Dean Letourneau, Boston's top prospect, as the asset Detroit would value most.

"They are not interested in draft picks," Friedman said on Sportsnet's Saturday Headlines, a sign Detroit had shifted toward young players in or near the NHL.

WATCH VIDEO: Bruins' Nikita Zadorov Fights Brady Tkachuk on Opening Faceoff

Elias Lindholm centered David Pastrnak and Morgan Geekie on the first line, with Zacha between Casey Mittelstadt and JJ Peterka on the second, in Boston's lineup against Washington on Saturday. James Hagens, one of the Bruins' young centers, missed a sixth straight game with a back injury.

Larkin averaged 21:41 of ice time this season, most among Red Wings forwards, and his cap hit is $8.7 million against the cap through 2030-31. The Globe reported he would have been Boston's top center, with Fraser Minten and Hagens behind him, ending a search for stable center play that dates to Patrice Bergeron and David Krejci.

On the man advantage, Larkin scored 34 goals in 74 games last season and averaged 3:16 of power-play time per game, according to RotoWire.

Montreal's biggest issue was depth at center, The Hockey News wrote in October, after Nick Suzuki's ironman streak ended at 546 games. Larkin now slots in behind Nick Suzuki, and Canadiens fans chanted "We want Larkin" at Bell Centre this season.

Dreger grouped the Bruins and Canadiens together early this month as clubs eager to get involved.

#2753. 4 things we learned from the Giants’ 23-18 victory over the Jaguars

Sunday was the day the New York Giants' Cinderella season carriage was going to turn back into the pumpkin of past season failures. That might yet happen – the road ahead is filled with difficult opponents. Today, though, the Giants for the first time established themselves as serious playoff contenders. They not only hung with the previously 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars, they actually dominated a good part of the game. Things got dicey in the second half as the Jaguars started to move the ball and tighten up their defense, but the Giants held on for a 23-18 victory that solidified their hold on first place (on a day when the Cowboys and Eagles both won) and perhaps more importantly, suggested that they might be more than just a competent team that can squeeze out victories over the NFL's bottom-dwellers. The NFL, which gambled that the Giants were for real by flexing their game into the national 4:30 window, won their bet with a thrilling game. What did we learn from the Giants' 23-18 win over Jacksonville?

There's been evidence of this since the start of the season, when Dennard Wilson's aggressive approach proved a welcome change from the passive Shane Bowen defense in the Giants' first game against Dallas. Still, most Giants games have been against poor to middling offensive teams, and when they faced a good offense, the Rams ran roughshod over them. Today it was the Jaguars' No. 5 scoring offense in the NFL, one that had put 30 or more points up 6 times already this season. The 18 points they scored against the Giants today was their second lowest of the season, trailing only the 12 points they scored in Denver (which has one of the NFL's best defenses). You have to credit the D as a whole. Trevor Lawrence did manage to put up 301 passing yards, but he only passed for 1 TD and was intercepted twice. Furthermore, the Jags' potent running game only had 77 yards, though admittedly star running back Bhayshul Tuten left with an injury mid-game.

The main reasons that was true today were:

Carter has been having what by some metrics would be considered a breakout season, ranking high in a number of pass rush metrics such as pass rush win rate and time to pressure. What has been lacking are sacks. Today, though, Carter sacked Lawrence twice and hit or at least pressured him a handful of other times. Carter's quickness and agility getting around blocks is other-worldly, and today he was finally rewarded for the work he's been doing. Forget the stats, when J.J. Watt seems impressed, that's good enough for me.

Part of the reason Carter was effective was that he wasn't alone. Kayvon Thobodeaux, as usual, did not get any sacks, but he was getting pressure from the other side as well (in addition to having a strong game against the run and intercepting a 2-point conversion attempt), and D.J. Reader was also getting pressure inside and had a sack of his own. There would have been more, but Lawrence is a pretty mobile QB for a guy his size, and the Giants had him running around a lot trying to escape and find someone downfield. The good thing is that the Giants did it without blitzing as much as they have in some recent games.

Part of the reason Lawrence had a long time to throw today (his longest of the season) was that the Giants did a pretty good job, all things considered, against the Jaguars' potent receiving corps. Parker Washington, who has become one of the NFL's best receivers, had 103 yards today, but that was on 17 targets, of which he only caught 8. Likewise, Jakobi Meyers had 85 yards, but again, on 10 targets of which he only caught four.

Much of that was due to Paulson Adebo. The Giants' big free agent signing last year, a disappointment then and relegated to the bench most of this year after being injured in Game 1, Adebo played perhaps his best game as a Giant. He held Washington to zero catches on three targets and Meyers to one 23-yard catch in five targets. He broke up four passes and also had an interception . Adebo entered the game after Greg Newsome left with an injury in the first quarter. If he is finally returning to his form of a couple of years ago when he was a Saint, that could be huge for the Giants, who will face some potent passing offenses in the coming weeks (he writes while watching Brock Purdy carve up the Vikings defense in the first half on Sunday Night Football).

Meanwhile, Deonte Banks continues to play great ball. Banks only gave up two receptions in 10 targets for 21 yards and had his second interception of the season. To me, this was his best game of the season, even though he had the game-saving pick-6 against Arizona. It is such a remarkable development after watching him languish the past two seasons. Part of Lawrence's problem tonight was that he couldn't find open receivers. If this continues this could be the Giants' best secondary since their 2022 playoff season.

In their first nine games, the Giants had five of them in which they gave up 163, 123, 202, 175, and 105 rushing yards. Today they gave up only 77 yards to a Jacksonville team that had rushed for over 100 yards in each of its last four games. The big news pre-game was that Darius Alexander was not active. That's quite a fall from grace for the former high third round draft pick who had given the Giants a little interior pass rush but who had been a liability against the run. In his place the Giants played Bobby Jamison-Travis, who's become a regular part of the rotation, and C.J. Okoye, who had missed the past three games. It's worth watching going forward to see how IDL snaps are distributed and whether the Giants are able to hold up against formidable rushing teams that are coming up such as the 49ers and Lions.

It can be frustrating to watch this Giants offense sometimes. J.J. McCarthy looked good early on, but he went downhill as the game progressed. To Matt Nagy's credit, the Giants finally dialed up some downfield passes for McCarthy today. Unfortunately, he was pretty awful on those passes – 0 for 5 beyond 20 yards, with most of them sailing well beyond the receiver. The Giants might have put up more than 30 if he'd had better touch downfield. He was pretty good on downfield passes as a Viking, so let's hope that today was just an aberration, because adding a downfield threat to their offense could be the difference between hanging with the good teams or being steamrolled by them.

The problem is that they need for J.J. to be good, because their rushing game has been suspect. The Giants do not have good run blockers, especially on the interior offensive line. John Harbaugh and Greg Roman have been searching all season for a bellcow to help their offense run at maximum efficiency. One problem is that all their running backs fumble. Another problem is that they tend to get injured. Another problem is that none of them are elite running backs even when they are at their best. Cam Skattebo got the call again tonight with Tyrone Tracy still injured…and he fumbled again tonight at a critical juncture. With the Giants already up 20-6, with a first down at the Jaguars' 33 and 4:01 left in the third quarter, once again Skattebo was stripped, his fifth of the season. Only a tackle by of all people J.J. McCarthy kept Antonio Johnson from returning it for a TD.

That was really a turning point in the game. It went from a solid, bordering on easy, victory for the Giants to a nail-biter. Jacksonville got the momentum, and by the 3:43 mark in the fourth quarter, Cam Little's field goal had gotten the Jaguars to within 23-18. Be honest – did you think the Giants were going to lose at that point?

I did. Then something remarkable happened. After Skattebo ran for 3 yards, McCarthy completed a 19-yard pass to Malachi Fields to get the Giants to the Jacksonville 43 yard line with 3:02 left. Then Skattebo ran for 5 yards. Then he ran for another 5 yards and a first down. Then the Giants were able to just run the clock to zeros with McCarthy kneel-downs and keepers. I don't think we've seen that since the opening game against Dallas. Overall the Giants finished with 77 rushing yards, but 33 of those were by McCarthy, basically on scrambles (he lost yardage on a couple of designed runs).

The question is why the Giants running game was finally able to run out the clock, and whether they can finally start to do that earlier in the game. They are not a terrible running team – entering today they were middle of the pack in team rushing yards. But they are eighth-worst in yards per carry. And we know that they want to be a running team. Today they had 3.1 yards per carry, pretty pedestrian.

Yet in the end they managed to run out the clock. So I can't decide whether they are or are not a bad running team. Hence the strikethrough on the section title above. Let's see how the rest of the season progresses.

#2752. WRU to discuss Anglo-Welsh move at crucial summit

Welsh Rugby Union chief executive (WRU) Abi Tierney says the prospect of Welsh clubs joining an expanded English league will be discussed in January at a crucial two-day summit meeting.

The event, which has been delayed after initially being planned for December, will include the WRU, regions and external stakeholders - with plans to cut a Welsh professional men's side also to be discussed.

"The summit is critical and we're creating it together," said Tierney, speaking after the WRU annual general meeting (AGM) at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff.

"It is everything. We'll have all the owners and their boards in a room, all the data and facts on the table, and we'll be saying, this is what it tells us."

The WRU announced they hope for both internal and external speakers, with three key areas set to be focused on; financial and commercial, pathways and performance, and what it takes to win.

Tierney admitted the recent prospect of trying to get into an Anglo-Welsh league will be discussed in January.

Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney confirmed earlier in November that the WRU had officially asked to join the English Prem and form an Anglo-Welsh league.

The Prem hopes to expand from 10 to 12 teams for the 2029-30 season, with a "long-term ambition" to grow further.

Prem Rugby has opened a registration process for teams to apply, with a 'request for information stage' now open until 1 February 2027 and which Welsh sides will now consider applying for.

Tierney was careful about what she said as she addressed the issue for the first time.

"Clearly, there's been a significant change in something that wasn't there a year ago that we've got to now take into account," she said.

"When we originally did the consultation last year, Anglo-Welsh wasn't an option. We tested it at the time and were told it wasn't an option.

"We've always said through this process that if other things change and options become available, it's beholden on us to explore all options.

"We've got a lot of water to go under the bridge to figure out what that combination is."

That includes discussions on continued involvement in the United Rugby Championship (URC), the five-country, cross-border competition to which the WRU is committed to providing four sides until 2028.

The WRU are a stakeholder in the competition alongside other member unions from Scotland, Ireland, Italy and South Africa.

"The relationship with the URC continues to be constructive," said Tierney.

"We're talking to them regularly. I think they understand on a human and inter-relational level. We continue to work as we always have."

When asked whether there was any threat of legal action towards the WRU, Tierney replied: "Yes, I think they'll be looking to make sure their interpretation of the contract, that we're clear on that. But we're going through that process."

Whether any Anglo-Welsh involvement affects the number of Welsh men's clubs that are retained remains to be seen.

The WRU has said it intends to drop a professional men's side by 2028.

With Cardiff and Dragons set to be granted the capital and east licences, Ospreys and Scarlets are competing to be the side in west Wales.

That decision is expected to be made in July 2027 with the summit outlining how the choice will be made.

Tierney was challenged at the AGM on the three-team plan that was unveiled in October 2025, while Ospreys and Scarlets have condemned the plan, saying Welsh rugby should keep four sides.

She responded that the WRU had not heard another plan, although she and director of rugby and head of elite performance Dave Reddin both stated they "were open to other options".

"If you read the consultation documents and responses to the consultation, everybody agreed radical change was needed and the majority agreed reducing the number of clubs," said Tierney.

"It's hard when the impact is real and it becomes one club.

"If you want a consensus, the only thing you're potentially going to have is continuing to do the same thing. I don't think that is going to put Wales on a sustainable footing."

Tierney says she is not giving up on trying to find a solution at the rugby summit.

"We've always said our preference would be to do this via consensus but if we can't get it, that doesn't mean we shouldn't do what we believe is our job as a national governing body," said Tierney.

"To do the right thing for the whole of Welsh rugby, as opposed to what's right for individual parts."

WRU publishes data on why west Wales team will be cut

Ospreys say report shows Wales must not cut teams

Abi Tierney became the first woman to be appointed as the WRU chief executive when she officially started the role in January 2024 [Huw Evans Picture Agency]

The number of clubs was just one issue that the WRU hierarchy were grilled on, in one of the most robust AGM's in recent memory.

Tierney was asked about whether she thought support would improve in west Wales if a region was cut.

When she suggested concentrating talent and resources could mean more successful clubs that attract support, she was labelled as "naive".

A question was also asked whether there would be more money for each of the three remaining sides.

The four regions currently get £6.5m each from the WRU with £26m given in total.

That overall figure will be reduced by £6m to £20m because of the current financial situation, which means a move to a three-club system will see each organisation having £6.7m each, just £200,000 more than the current amount the four teams get.

Tierney was faced with a question about the internal culture within the WRU and whether its own staff have confidence in the governing body's executive leadership.

She also chose not to respond to a query about comments made by former president and Welsh rugby legend Sir Gerald Davies, who criticised the current WRU leadership in the aftermath of the victory against New Zealand.

While there was more public AGM scrutiny from the clubs than in recent years, Tierney - who remarked during the meeting that fighting and toxicity was destroying Welsh rugby - believes the WRU do have silent support.

She said: "I got about 30 people afterwards coming up to me, saying 'you've got our support, please keep going'.

"That's almost more important because some of those people I have huge amounts of respect for and engage with on a regular basis.

"I reflect on why they didn't feel able to say that in the room because some people don't want to put their hand up in front of 300 people.

"There's quite a lot of people who have had enough of the negativity."

Tierney is not expecting another extraordinary general meeting (EGM) after one was called in April by one of the Welsh districts.

"I don't think they've got the support for it but if that group wants to do that, then OK," she said.

"It's relentless and you constantly feel the negativity, it's exhausting."

Tierney, Reddin, chief financial officer Gavin Marshall and community boss Geraint John gave presentations before a lively one-hour question and answer session where the quartet were scrutinised.

Reddin fielded a question about why had the WRU had abandoned north Wales, something he refuted.

After the meeting, Tierney praised Reddin after he outlined his performance and pathways vision.

"Dave is a genius, the way he builds systems and structures," she said.

"I don't think I had realised just what little we had there before he came in.

"It was held together by brilliant people doing what they possibly could.

"We had no systems and structure in place and Dave is literally building it bit by bit from the bottom up, which will last for a generation."

Tierney added: "Our banks have seen Dave's detailed presentation and they back it.

"They believe that is what is going to deliver a sustainable return on investment.

"If we get the national men's team performing successfully and grow the women's game, the banks buy into it, based on their global experience of what he is putting in place.

"We are taking these two years to build the pathway, the new national academy system and player development centres, to get everything in place.

"So when we land on the number of clubs and in which competition we're in, we'll have that system beneath us."

Marshall was asked about the £18m loss the WRU posted recently and why he initially gave a positive outlook in May about the governing body's finances before outlining the worrying situation a few months later.

"Gavin is one of the best finance people I have worked with and I think we are a good combination," said Tierney.

"I am naturally an optimist and ambitious, while he is a bit more of a realist and pessimist.

"He is a good operator and he has been a CEO before, so he gets the broader operations."

'WRU like Man Utd' but Davies backs Faulkner

Cutting team will not address WRU £18m loss - Ospreys

Lyndon Faulkner is the nephew of former Wales prop Charlie [Huw Evans Picture Agency]

New chair Lyndon Faulkner will oversee the WRU board as he officially starts his role after replacing Richard Collier-Keywood.

Faulkner concluded the meeting by warning of the grim financial situation the WRU faces and promising an urgency for change and accountability from the organisation.

He received the warmest applause of the meeting and it was evident he resonated with the clubs, given his background as a former Newport and Pontypool forward who became a successful businessman in the United States of America.

Faulkner has previously insisted he is no WRU yes man but will oversee the final decision on professional rugby over the next six months.

"We'll deal with that based on the facts," said Faulkner.

"The good news is we've got all four regions in at the highest level, as part of the discussion.

"There are things that weren't previously on the table. Things will unfold and we've got a little bit of time.

"It's a pity uncertainty is out there while we are deliberating on what our options are, because that doesn't help, but we are where we are."

#2751. Prediction markets outlook for stocks in 2026 dims amid AI sell-off

As stocks continue their tech-driven sell-off, prediction markets traders are seeing a bleaker outlook for the remainder of the year.

On platform Kalshi, speculators place just 6% odds that the S&P 500 will cross 8,000 in 2026. On Oct. 13, those odds were as high as 72%.

Contracts ask traders if the S&P 500 will go above various levels in 2026, and they're resolved using data from S&P Dow Jones Indices.

On Friday, the Nasdaq Composite turned negative for the year as investors continued to dump tech stocks, primarily those with exposure to the artificial intelligence build-out. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500 fell into correction territory, too.

The S&P 500 has slashed its year-to-date gain to just over 2%.

The Stock Trader's Almanac in a Thursday note broadly agreed that the hopes for a December rally are fading, with the caveat that a "Santa rally" could still appear at the end of the year.

"The market is under pressure and more downside can't be ruled out," the note said.

The Stock Trader's Almanac sees 2026 following the year-end pattern of 2018, when the Federal Reserve was in a tightening cycle in a midterm year. The Fed is widely expected to hike rates at its December meeting.

In that scenario, the Stock Trader's Almanac thinks more churn is to come. "The low is more likely in mid- to late December than this week."

#2749. 49ers’ Emotional Scene After Former WVU Star Suffers Gruesome Injury

ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 25: Colton McKivitz #68 of the San Francisco 49ers blocks against the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty

The West Virginia Mountaineers were fortunate to have Colton McKivitz in Morgantown for five years. Since leaving the program, the former WVU offensive lineman has built a successful career with the San Francisco 49ers, becoming a dependable presence on their offensive line. Unfortunately, Sunday night's game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City brought a frightening moment for the veteran.

With approximately six minutes remaining in the second quarter, McKivitz appeared to suffer a serious leg injury when his leg became trapped and twisted awkwardly during a play. The scene was difficult to watch, and the reaction from his teammates showed just how much the 30-year-old means to San Francisco.

Veteran tackle Trent Williams appeared emotional as medical personnel attended to McKivitz. Other 49ers players reportedly threw their helmets in frustration, while the crowd applauded as the former Mountaineer was carted off the field.

GettyATLANTA, GEORGIA – OCTOBER 25: Colton McKivitz #68 of the San Francisco 49ers blocks against the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images)

At the time of writing, the exact nature and severity of McKivitz's injury had not been confirmed. The appearance of the play was concerning, but any diagnosis will have to come from the team's medical evaluation.

Long before McKivitz established himself in the NFL, he earned that same respect at West Virginia. He spent the 2015 through 2019 seasons with the Mountaineers, appearing in 50 games and making 47 starts.

His senior season was particularly impressive. McKivitz started every game at left tackle in 2019, earning first-team All-Big 12 recognition and sharing the conference's Offensive Lineman of the Year award. He also received All-America honors, finishing his college career as one of the program's most accomplished recent linemen.

San Francisco selected McKivitz in the fifth round of the 2020 NFL draft. He gradually worked his way into a larger role, eventually becoming a regular starter. The 49ers rewarded that development with a three-year contract extension in September 2025, keeping him under contract through 2028.

Football injuries can change the mood of a stadium in seconds. That appeared to happen Sunday when teammates gathered around McKivitz and the crowd recognized the seriousness of the moment.

For West Virginia supporters, this wasn't simply another NFL injury involving an unfamiliar player. McKivitz spent years representing the Mountaineers, developing into an award-winning offensive lineman before earning his place in professional football.

His durability has been a major part of that journey, which makes watching him leave the field especially difficult. There will be time to evaluate what the injury means for San Francisco's offensive line once more information becomes available.

For now, the focus is on McKivitz's health. Mountaineers fans and 49ers teammates alike will be hoping for encouraging news about a player who has earned respect at every stop.

#2745. ‘It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround

'It worked every time': How Sixers found a clutch answer at shootaround originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers created their two cleanest late-game looks several hours before they needed them.

During Wednesday morning's shootaround in Orlando, Nick Nurse had the Sixers work on offensive material they had not consistently used this season. They tested one of those actions during the first half, returned to it throughout the closing minutes and watched it produce the shots they needed to complete a 17-point comeback.

"We worked on some stuff this morning that we hadn't used before, and they ran all that stuff very, very well and very calmly and with composure," Nurse told reporters.

The Sixers have earned six of their 13 wins after trailing by double digits. They are also 11-0 in games that reached clutch time.

Relying on comebacks is not a sustainable plan. The repeated late-game situations, however, have forced a new roster to respond to different lineups, coverages and responsibilities while the season is still young.

Each close finish gives Nurse more information about which players and actions hold up when possessions tighten. Wednesday gave him a new option.

Anfernee Simons' clinching three in the Sixers' 121-116 win over the Magic was the final result of that preparation.

"That last play, we ran that play in the first half," Simons said. "We worked it a couple of times, and in the second half we ran that play every single time down the stretch, and it worked every time.

"It was a play we ran through. [It's gratifying] especially when it's working consistently and you're getting different shots out of it and the opposing team just don't know what to do.

"We just continue to run the play and get the open shots we need."

NBC Sports Philadelphia video producer and Sixers Talk podcast co-host Kevin Rice broke down how the Sixers used its different options to keep Orlando guessing.

The action begins with two players stationed near the elbows. A player on the opposite elbow then sets a screen for the player up top, who receives the ball while moving around it.

The Sixers ran the set three consecutive times during the first half. None of the possessions reached the primary option. Each still produced a quality opportunity.

On the first, Joel Embiid cleared LeBron James out of the area and directed Simons around him for a dribble handoff. Simons received an open three-point look.

Orlando took away the handoff the next time down but left Embiid one-on-one against Wendell Carter Jr. Embiid created enough room to retrieve his own miss and convert an and-one opportunity.

The third attempt pulled Orlando's defense into the paint. Two passes moved the ball through the collapsing coverage and created an open three for VJ Edgecombe.

"We had a little thing where he comes flying off behind Joel, and he doesn't get to do that that much, right?" Nurse said of Simons. "So tonight he gets the opportunity to do it, and it was very good for us on a number of plays."

The Sixers changed the action late without abandoning its initial Horns alignment. Simons moved through the lane to help form a Spain pick-and-roll involving James and Embiid.

On the first late possession, Simons remained near the play after James gained a matchup against Carter. Orlando struggled to sort out its assignments, leaving James open for a 19-foot jumper with 54.8 seconds remaining.

After Jalen Suggs made one of two free throws, the Sixers returned to the same setup. This time, Simons relocated to the left corner after James drew Carter on a switch.

James drove into the paint. Suggs lost track of Simons while responding to the penetration, and James sent the ball toward the corner.

Simons buried the open three to give the Sixers a 119-113 lead with 15 seconds left.

"Bron just penetrated the paint," Simons said. "It kind of got some confusion, and when I was on the dunker and kind of spaced out to the corner, I ended up finding myself wide open for the three, and Bron found me."

The Sixers entered the night without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, their two leading scorers. Simons made his first start with Philadelphia and recorded 18 points in the city where he grew up.

His final basket also illustrated why Nurse believes the Sixers have more to uncover with him.

"When he's out there, they gotta be really careful," Nurse said. "So I think there's some drives he creates, and just about every time he lets it go, whether he's on balance or not, you think it's going in, and that is a big deal. Like, that is a big deal.

"And again, I think we're still a ways away from really unlocking him to being even more part of some of the things we can do with him to create more shots."

Philadelphia is now 11-0 in clutch games. The finish in Orlando provided a more specific explanation than experience or shot-making alone.

The Sixers installed a set in the morning, explored its counters and trusted it when the game tightened. James supplied the patience to read Orlando's coverage. Embiid occupied the middle of the action. Simons moved without the ball, and Edgecombe remained ready to shoot.

James said his heart rate drops when close games increase the pressure on everyone else.

"I mean, experience," James said. "A guy that's seen every situation this league has to offer. It's nothing I haven't seen. And, you know, in the moments where people's heart rate goes up or anxiety goes up, mine is pretty low. It's actually lower, you know."

The Sixers still have more actions and reads to learn as Nurse becomes familiar with his new personnel, but their latest win showed their innate ability to adapt in big moments.

"I think we're still a long ways away from knowing all the reads and all that stuff because it's just a little early, right?" Nurse said.

#2744. The Nasdaq is in freefall. Here's one stock to look at

I asked Claude after Friday's close what I should do about the tanking stock market. Its advice was surprisingly useful: avoid panic selling and look for opportunities. A 40 VIX, which it touched Friday, might provide those opportunities. Specifically, a higher VIX (higher options premiums) signals fear, but it also creates an opportunity to sell elevated premium in some premium stocks, like Amazon.

Amazon's cloud business is growing at its fastest pace in nearly five years. AWS revenue rose 39.3% YoY in the third quarter, and management reported a $578 billion backlog. Trailing 12-month operating cash flow rose 29% to $168.3 billion. However, infrastructure investment accelerated, resulting in more than $42 billion in negative cash flow. The competing forces of accelerating growth and the cost of supplying it could keep the stock in its range over the next four weeks. Its shares are only off 14% from its recent highs, comparatively better than the Nasdaq Composite's near 19% decline.

AWS demand supports the lower end of the range. The backlog gives Amazon a basis for adding capacity even as investors scrutinize the cash cost. Cash spending could temper an upside rerating.

The next leg higher may require evidence that new capacity can earn attractive returns at this scale, and that evidence may be in short supply over the next couple of months.

#2741. Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3

Observations after Sixers survive Bucks' late surge, reach 14-3 originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers survived the Bucks' late surge and reached 14-3 on the season Saturday afternoon with a 132-129 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Joel Embiid had 26 points, a season-high 17 rebounds and nine assists for the Sixers.

LeBron James (21 points), Tyrese Maxey (17 points) and Anfernee Simons (18) were among the seven Sixers to score in double figures.

The Sixers were down Jaylen Brown (left hamstring strain), Dean Wade (left hamstring tightness/soreness), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear).

Next up for the Sixers is a Monday night meeting with the Trail Blazers. Here are observations on their victory over the Bucks:

Maxey returned to the Sixers' starting five after missing the team's comeback win Wednesday over the Magic with right foot soreness. He was joined by VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, James and Embiid.

James threw down a dunk on the day's first play. Embiid then dished to a cutting Edgecombe for a layup that put the Sixers up 4-0.

The Bucks quickly found a foothold in the game.

Embiid missed his first four shots, including two that were swatted by Myles Turner. Maxey began 1 for 5 from the floor. Herro canned a three-pointer to give Milwaukee a 15-8 lead.

The Sixers entered the game with a minus-13.2 net rating in first quarters, which ranked 28th in the NBA. They faced a 30-29 deficit after Saturday's first period.

Even with Maxey available again, Labaron Philon Jr. deservingly stayed in the Sixers' rotation following an excellent outing in Orlando.

He scored two points in six first-half minutes. The 20-year-old made a rookie mistake at the tail end of the first quarter, fouling Herro on a three-point attempt.

Dominick Barlow checked in for his first action of the season with 2:51 remaining in the first quarter. He'd been sidelined for the Sixers' first 16 games because of a lower back stress reaction.

Barlow scored his first points early in the second quarter when he tipped in a Maxey miss. He then teamed up with James in crowd-pleasing style, sprinting ahead of the pack on a fast break and flushing home the 22-time All-Star's long-distance lob.

The afternoon was not devoid of rust for Barlow. Shortly after that alley-oop, he grabbed an offensive rebound, dribbled out to the perimeter and fired an open three-pointer … which he air balled short.

To Barlow's credit, he took another three early in the fourth quarter and drained it. He logged 11 minutes and was quite productive, tallying 12 points on 5-for-6 shooting and four rebounds.

"It felt great," Barlow said of his three. "Got to shoot the ball with confidence. … I've obviously got to get a game feel; I've been missing that. But I worked too hard (in the offseason) to not shoot the ball when I'm open."

Kyle Kuzma hit a three late in the second quarter to build the Bucks' lead to 59-52. After Sixers head coach Nick Nurse's timeout, the team closed the first half on a 8-0 run featuring an Embiid dunk.

The Sixers went just 3 for 16 from long range in the first half, but their low-turnover ways helped mitigate those shooting struggles.

They committed a single turnover in the first half and finished with four giveaways. That's tied for their lowest ever on record in a single game. The Sixers have the NBA's lowest turnover percentage outside of garbage time, according to Cleaning the Glass.

"No matter who you're playing against, teams try to turn you over, they try to speed you up," James said. "Us taking care of the ball, that's a lot of the reason why we won this game."

The Sixers' shooters were bound to start sinking some open looks eventually. Simons, Caldwell-Pope and Edgecombe all made threes late in the third quarter and the team's lead grew as high as 13 points.

Thanks largely to Herro's individuals exploits, the Bucks stayed competitive. AJ Green buried a corner three to cut Milwaukee's deficit to 106-103 with 8:10 to go in the game.

James sought out his shot much more following the Sixers' timeout and did so with great success. He scored four buckets inside over the next four minutes, including a big slam that put the Sixers up 121-112.

It appeared the main questions left were whether Embiid could reach a triple-double and just how many points Herro would rack up.

However, the Bucks forced the Sixers to work down the stretch. Herro got to the 50-point milestone and trimmed the Sixers' lead to two points when he converted a layup with 19.2 seconds left.

The Sixers safely navigated to the final buzzer by the slimmest of margins. Embiid made four late free throws and everyone on the Sixers' sideline was relieved to see that Herro hadn't quite released his jumper in time.

"I try not to complain too much about any win in this league," Nurse said. "The message is we've got to finish a little better."

#2740. Vancouver Whitecaps set MLS Cup tone after dominant Game 1 victory

VANCOUVER, BC — If the pre-game violin rendition of "Freed From Desire" wasn't enough to set the tone for the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs in Vancouver, the team certainly did on the pitch over the course of 90 minutes Sunday at BC Place.

With goals from Édier Ocampo and Bruno Caicedo, paired with five saves from Yohei Takaoka, Vancouver Whitecaps FC picked up a 2-0 win over Real Salt Lake to open their Round One, Best-of-3 series and hopeful MLS Cup run.

In a slate of Game 1 matches that saw three top seeds, including Supporters' Shield winners Nashville SC and reigning MLS Cup champions Inter Miami, falter to lower-seeded opposition, the Whitecaps got the job done.

Crisis averted, even if there wasn't much of one to begin with.

"We played 34 games, but we know that in one playoff game things can be thrown upside down and that's how it is, so you have to be prepared for way more scenarios," said head coach Jesper Sørensen after the match.

"We came out strong and with a lot of energy, and I think the atmosphere also animated the players... we made our point on the pitch."

A year after losing in MLS Cup presented by Audi to Miami, the Whitecaps came into Sunday knowing the pomp and circumstance of a home playoff game in front of the BC Place faithful.

Their "hunger," as Thomas Müller described it ahead of the match, is also teeming, and 31,106 fans packed BC Place to witness what many in the market hope will be another lengthy playoff run.

With Nashville on the brink of elimination against FC Cincinnati, dreams of a home MLS Cup are alive among fans, even as they know the road ahead is long.

"It's always really beautiful," Ocampo said through a translator. "The support of the fans is key, and I think they're the 12th player on the pitch for us. We know we didn't get the job done last year, but we really want to get the job done this year. We need to do it for the fans."

While Ocampo and Caicedo got on the scoresheet, captain Ryan Gauld embraced the pressure of starting the postseason after a lengthy injury held him out of most of last year's run.

After netting 6g/5a in 20 games, and with his injury behind him, he delivered in commanding fashion.

"In the last few weeks, he's had that power in his step again that he can really separate himself," added Sørensen of Gauld. "He can make it through the pressure in a different way, and we all know about his skills and his technical abilities."

Vancouver now heads to America First Field on Friday (10 pm ET | Apple TV), hoping to complete the sweep and set up a home Western Conference Final against either the San Jose Earthquakes or the Houston Dynamo.

If things go their way, it could also prove to be the only road game of the playoffs, with the only other potential away match being an MLS Cup showdown against Nashville at GEODIS Park Dec. 18.

"We have a lot of guys who were part of the group that lost the final last year," said defender Ralph Priso after the clean sheet. "This is what we play all season, big moments where everything matters because we want to be champions."

"We were so close, and now we just want to get back to that, but obviously to get there, we need to take care of each game."

#2737. Vikings' defense has first poor outing of season as 49ers dominate in easy win

Kirk Cousins of the Minnesota Vikings is hit by Nick Bosa of the San Francisco 49ers. (Photo by Manuel Velasquez/Getty Images)

The Minnesota Vikings had high hopes after last week, when Kirk Cousins joined the team and they blew out the Green Bay Packers. With the Vikings' defense playing very well yet again and Cousins providing much better play at quarterback in his first game with Minnesota after coming over in a trade, entering the Super Bowl discussion seemed reasonable.

Sunday night was a good time to measure where the Vikings stood in the NFC hierarchy. And they found out there's a big gap between them and the San Francisco 49ers.

The 49ers have looked like a Super Bowl contender since Week 1 when they blew out the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, and that domination continued in Mexico City on Sunday night. The 49ers handled the Vikings with surprising ease. They improved to 9-1 with a 35-10 win.

The Vikings (7-3) are still in good shape. But their defense finally showed some vulnerability and their offense took a step back from the first game with Cousins. Minnesota could still win the NFC North and make a deep playoff run, but Sunday showed there's a long way to go to reach the 49ers' level.

The Vikings' defense was in trouble from the first drive. The 49ers moved the ball without any problem downfield and then tight end George Kittle scored on a 17-yard touchdown. The ease in which the 49ers moved the ball was surprising because nobody had been able to move it like that on the Vikings. The Vikings were so dominant, they held the Bears and their explosive offense to three points in Week 2. But the Vikings had no answers for the 49ers.

Coordinator Brian Flores brings extra pass rushers way more than any other defense in the NFL, and once the 49ers figured out how to combat that by Brock Purdy getting the ball out quickly, Minnesota's defense wasn't so scary anymore.

The 49ers scored touchdowns on three of their first four drives. Minnesota hadn't allowed more than 23 points in a game all season and the 49ers had 21 before halftime when Mike Evans made a great catch in the end zone, though there was a question if he had control with both feet down. It didn't matter because the touchdown call stood and at that point the Vikings were in danger of the game slipping away.

Then Cousins made a mistake before halftime that practically finished the game before halftime.

The Vikings trailed 21-10 when 49ers safety Ji'Ayir Brown read Cousins and the Vikings' play perfectly and jumped in front of a pass intended for Tai Felton. Brown picked it off and had an easy 18-yard return for the touchdown.

Minnesota's defense having its troubles with Purdy and the 49ers was the key to the game but the Vikings' offense struggled too. They got a touchdown in the first quarter and didn't get another the rest of the game.

The Vikings are known for pressuring quarterbacks, but it was the 49ers who had constant pressure on Cousins. NBC's cameras found Cousins in an animated discussion with tackle Brian O'Neill on the sideline, seemingly telling O'Neill he was being hit every play. Without much of a running game or protection on pass plays, it was tough for Cousins to function.

The Vikings are still one of the NFL's better teams. They just had a tough matchup against a 49ers team that has a great argument as the best in the NFL. There's a long way to go in the season. That gives Minnesota time to figure out how it can match up better with San Francisco the next time, if they happen to meet in the playoffs.

And we're officially done in Mexico City. The 49ers are now a near-perfect 9-1 after the win, which marked their third straight.

The Vikings hold a 7-3 record, and have lost three of their last four. They are 1-1 now with Kirk Cousins as a starter after the deadline trade.

Carson Wentz is in for the Vikings now, and Brock Purdy's day is done, too, as we hit the two mintue warning.

The 49ers couldn't extend their drive to kill the game here, and got stopped on third after Deebo Samuel was stopped a few yards short of the first.

Minnesota will take back over with 3:46 to go, but this one is over.

The Vikings got all the way to the SF 20, but their attempt on fourth down was stopped just a few yards short of the line to gain.

They needed a touchdown there to stay alive. Instead, Kirk Cousins is headed back to the sidelines down by 25 with just 8:16 to go.

And that should do it. Christian McCaffery punched in a 6-yard score one play after making his first catch of the night, and the 49ers are now up 35-10.

That was a 98 yard drive for San Francisco.

It was a scoreless third period, but San Francisco is knocking on the red zone looking to extend its lead.

If they can add seven more here, this game will essentially be over. The Vikings absolutely need a stop.

The 49ers were all over Tai Felton there to break up the pass, and the Vikings will now have to punt. That was a long 10-play drive, but htey only made it 36 yards before having to punt.

Minnesota will have to get points on the board here soon if it's going to mount a comeback.

The Vikings defense has responded yet again. They forced a quck three-and-out, and put too much pressure on Brock Purdy in the backfield there on third down for him to get a good throw off.

Minnesota will get another shot with the ball here in the second half.

Justin Jefferson looked like he had a path to the end zone there, but he did not have a firm grip on the ball at all. Deommodore Lenoir easily punched the ball out of his hands to force the early turnover.

San Francisco has suddenly taken back over. That's not the start Minnesota needed.

The Vikings have received the kick, and the second half is underway. We'll see if they can rally here.

The 49ers weren't able to score there, but they've been dominating so far tonight in Mexico City. Brock Purdy has thrown for 176 yards and three touchdowns already, two of which went to George Kittle.

Minnesota will get the ball to start the second half. The Vikings attempted a 71-yard field goal just before half, but it was just barely short. That was only the 10th 70+ yard attempt in NFL history.

San Francisco will have a chance to put up more points before half. The 49ers forced a quick three-and-out there, so the Vikings will have to put with 68 seconds left before the break.

One more touchdown before half would blow this game wide open.

What a turn for the 49ers! On the first play after Mike Evans' touchdown, Ji'Ayir Brown jumped up and intercepted Kirk Cousins to set up an easy trot into the end zone.

What a grab from Mike Evans! Brock Purdy found him in the back corner, and he hauled that ball in with just one hand perfectly.

The 49ers lead 21-10 now with 2:09 left in the half.

Colton McKivitz went down with what appears to be a significant ankle injury. His ankle was going off the wrong direction, and teammate Trent Williams slammed his helmet there after seeing it up close.

He's being carted off now, and the entire 49ers team came over to see him off.

The Vikings had to settle for a 48-yard field goal there after their drive stalled out. They converted on fourth-and-short earlier to keep it alive, too.

But points are points. The 49ers lead 14-10 now with 6:48 left in the half.

George Kittle had to power through Harrison Smith to make the grab, but he's now got his second touchdown of the night. What a catch.

The 49ers lead 14-7 now early in the second.

We're all tied up after the first quarter in Mexico City, but the 49ers are driving once again. Brock Purdy just found Mike Evans for a 34-yard gain right up the middle, and they're in the red zone.

Just like that, the Vikings have tied this game up. Aaron Jones capped the nine-play drive with an 11-yard touchdown run up the left side.

Nick Bosa nearly got his first sack of the season on Kirk Cousins on the play right before the score, too. But instead, he was hit with a penalty for drilling Cousins in the backfield.

It's 7-7 now with 1:13 left in the first.

#2736. Colton McKivitz Injury Update: $45 Million 49ers OT Suffers Gruesome Leg Injury

The San Francisco 49ers lost a critical piece of their offense during Sunday night's Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, when starting right offensive tackle Colton McKivitz suffered a gruesome lower-leg injury in the first half.

NBC cameras couldn't cut away before a shot came through of McKivitz on the ground at Estadio Balnorte, giving viewers a quick glimpse of what just happened to his lower left leg — an image that will be hard to forget.

"The reactions to Colton McKivitz's injury tells you everything you need to know," NFL Network's Mike Garafolo wrote on X. "Air cast for the 49ers' RT too. Brutal for the Niners, as Vederian Lowe takes over on the right side."

"Colton McKivitz suffered a Left ankle/fibula fracture," Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on his official X account. "Huge loss to the 49ers OL, he's been very solid at RT."

SNF color commentator Cris Collinsworth quickly pointed out that McKivitz, who signed a 3-year, $45 million contract extension before the 2025 season, had not given up a sack this season and had played in 77 consecutive games for the 49ers.

"Trent Williams just gave McKivitz a long hug and, presumably, some words of encouragement," ESPN's Nick Wagoner wrote on X. "Brutal injury for a player who has been so good for the 49ers this year."

The 49ers took a 20-10 lead on the same drive, with a touchdown pass from quarterback Brock Purdy to wide receiver Mike Evans, then went up 27-10 on the Vikings' ensuing possession on an interception return for a touchdown by 49ers free safety Ji'Ayir Brown.

McKivitz has truly been playing the best football of his career this season.

According to Pro Football Focus, McKivitz's 82.8 overall grade through the first 9 games of the season puts him 7th out of 72 eligible players at his position.

"Awful injury to Colton McKivitz, who was having a career year," ESPN's Ben Solak wrote on X. "Really big loss for the 49ers."

"Colton McKivitz is one of the best right tackles in the league, and it looks like this is a bad (injury)," NBC Sports' Matt Maiocco wrote on X.

McKivitz, 6-foot-6 and 301 pounds, was the Big 12 Co-Offensive Lineman of the Year in 2019 at West Virginia and was also named All-American and a 2-time All-Big 12 pick.

The 49ers selected McKivitz in the 5th round (No. 153 overall) in the 2020 NFL Draft. He only started 5 games over his first 3 seasons with the 49ers before taking over as the full-time starter at right offensive tackle in 2023, when Mike McGlinchey left to sign with the Denver Broncos in free agency.

McKivitz, 30, has started every game for the 49ers since 2023, and his current contract will bring his career earnings to $55.9 million and runs through 2028.

#2735. James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers

James sees a lot to like — and improve — for East-leading Sixers originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

LeBron James likes to refer to the NBA season as a "marathon."

A few miles in, the Sixers lead the Eastern Conference pack.

With 17 regular-season contests down of 82, the team sits at 14-3, which is 2.5 games ahead of the second-seeded Celtics. The Sixers squeaked out their latest win, a 132-129 decision Saturday over the cellar-dwelling Bucks, but the bottom line is they've become accustomed to finding many routes to victory.

"We want to build habits," James said. "We want to try to take steps forward every game that we get the opportunity. I know sometimes it doesn't happen that way, but we want to do it.

"We want to strive to be as great as we can offensively, defensively and on special teams. A win is a win, but there's ways to win and ways to try to continue to build habits over the course of a marathon."

All sorts of Sixers games have gone down to the wire and they've won every single one.

The team is an incredible 12-0 in clutch situations, defined as games with a point differential of five or under in the final five minutes. The Sixers rank third in the NBA in clutch offensive rating (140.3) and third in clutch net rating (plus-42.0).

"It's good to build that part of our game," James said. "Obviously, we wanted to close the game out a lot better. But a team like that, we know they're going to be scrappy. They're going to play as hard as they can for 48 minutes. … We can learn from that."

James was the centerpiece of the Sixers' fourth-quarter offense Saturday. He scored 13 of his 21 points between the 7:46 and 3:13 mark of the fourth.

The four-time MVP got two buckets on no-nonsense drives and another on an after-timeout isolation hoop over rookie Brayden Burries. James also scored three times on a designed Horns action where he brought the ball up, used Tyrese Maxey's back screen at the elbow and caused serious problems for Milwaukee in the paint.

"We continue to add things to the half-court offense and also to the late-game package," Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. "That's something we added a few game ago. It's one of those things where, especially if we're in the bonus, we've got some big bodies that can cut down the lane and have feel for timing. It was working. Just keep going to it."

James has grown in comfort with Nurse's coaching style. He knows the Sixers expect him to be a de facto coach on the floor, too.

"I'm just trying to be there for the team in any capacity they want," he said. "Just trying to be an extension of his calls and his commands out there on the floor. Trying to make his life and his job a little bit easier as well.

"But it's been great, not only with him but the whole coaching staff. They've welcomed me with open arms and allowed me to kind of be the voice for the team every day, and take that responsibility."

After a tremendous first impression defensively and some subpar offensive nights, the Sixers' numbers have recently evened out.

The team is 12th in offensive rating outside of garbage time and 12th in defensive rating, per Cleaning the Glass. In essence, the Sixers have been a bit above average on both ends of the floor and downright brilliant in the closing minutes.

It's all added up to an early lead in a very long race.

"I think we've bought into the pass," James said. "We have so many guys that can score the ball at elite levels. … In order for us to be a super-complete team, I think the power of the pass is very infectious. And it's also key for our other guys, to make sure they feel in a rhythm and they feel confident. We've done that from Day 1 and I think it's gotten better and better. … And I think our defense has been really good for the majority of the season.

"(Today) it wasn't so great, but we've been very good defensively throughout the course of the season. … I don't want to say there's anything bad. There's so many things for us to do better for sure. There's games where we can defensive rebound a lot better and there's games where we can not turn the ball over (as much). And there's games where we can be a little more phsyical defensively at the point of attack like (today).

"I wouldn't say anything has been bad, though. That's a good thing. We want to continue to have room for improvement and we don't want to be great in November. That would be weird."
